hook.text: A history student organized her notes as nested bullet points: main topics, subtopics, and details.

buildup.text: The outlining method uses indentation to show hierarchy: main ideas at the left, supporting details indented beneath.

discovery.text: This method excels when the material has clear structure: lectures with sections, textbooks with chapter outlines.

twist.text: It struggles with non-linear content. When a speaker jumps between topics, the outline breaks and reorganization.

climax.text: Use outlining for structured content. If the source has no clear hierarchy, switch to a more flexible method.

punchline.text: Structured source? Outline it. Chaos? Use another method.

quiz.question: When does the outlining method work best?
options: When the material is creative and unstructured
When the material has clear hierarchical structure
When you need to capture visual information
